listing.description_html:
Find out whether a refinance really pays: monthly savings, break-even month, and the true cost difference over the years you will actually keep the loan.

Most quick calculators stop at the monthly saving. This workbook also finds the break-even month, and compares the two loans over the period you expect to keep the loan, counting the payments made and the balance still owed at the end, so a longer new term cannot hide its cost.

What's included

  • Monthly payment for your current loan and the new offer
  • Break-even month: when the closing costs are paid back by the monthly saving
  • Net benefit over the years you will actually keep the loan, counting the balance still owed
  • Option to pay closing costs in cash or roll them into the new loan
  • Year by Year sheet: both balances and the running advantage for ten years
  • PDF guide with a worked example and a field-by-field reference

Who it's for

  • Homeowners comparing a refinance offer with their current mortgage
  • Borrowers deciding between paying closing costs in cash or rolling them into the loan
  • Anyone comparing two fixed-rate loan offers on the same balance
  • Small landlords reviewing refinancing on a rental property

You get: refinance_break_even_calculator.xlsx (Inputs, Comparison, Year by Year) and this guide.

Works in Excel 2016 or later, Excel for Mac and Excel on the web; opens in Google Sheets and LibreOffice.

This workbook is a comparison tool, not financial, lending or tax advice. It uses fixed-rate payment math and the figures you enter; check any loan decision against your lender's official Loan Estimate and with a qualified adviser.
